claims.text: The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) introduced a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) framework for the Unified Payments Interface (UPI) effective from October 15.
Under the new NPCI framework, customers will pay no charges for making UPI payments regardless of transaction value.
Merchants receiving UPI payments above Rs 2,000 in a single transaction will be levied a 0.4% Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), with an upper cap of Rs 300.
The Finance Ministry stated that MDR fees collected will be distributed among payment ecosystem participants, including banks and app providers, to support operations and expansion.
Person-to-person UPI transfers account for 70% of total UPI transaction value and will remain completely free for individuals.
Small merchants receiving up to Rs 1 lakh per month will pay no fees on incoming UPI payments.
A flat MDR rate of Rs 5 will apply to UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 in essential sectors including railways, telecommunications, insurance, fuel, and agricultural inputs.
Capital market UPI transactions for mutual funds, securities, stockbrokers, and dealers will attract an MDR of 0.02%, capped at Rs 300 per transaction.
The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) issued a circular on Tuesday, September 15, 2026, introducing the 0.4% MDR on UPI merchant transactions over Rs 2,000.
Person-to-person UPI transactions constitute 37% of total UPI transaction volume and 70% of transaction value.
The Indian government stated that data analysis shows only 4% of merchant UPI transactions will be impacted by the introduction of the MDR.
A dedicated fund for promoting UPI usage by small merchants will be established using 5% of total MDR collections.
Opposition parties in India criticized the government's decision to levy a 0.4% MDR on UPI merchant payments above Rs 2,000, calling it the 'Modi tax'.
Congress media head Pawan Khera stated that Prime Minister Narendra Modi popularised UPI for a cashless economy and is now taxing people for using it.
Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi surrendered to American pressure after US payment companies opposed India's zero-MDR policy.
Essential sectors subject to the flat Rs 5 MDR account for nearly 17% of person-to-merchant UPI transaction volume and around 46% of transaction value.
The Union Ministry of Finance issued the notification regarding UPI merchant charges under Section 10A of the 2007 Payment and Settlement Systems Act.
In August 2026, Parliament passed the 2026 Taxation and Other Laws Amendment Bill, which amended the 2007 Payment and Settlement Systems Act to allow charges on UPI and RuPay debit card payments.
According to NPCI, standard credit card Merchant Discount Rates typically range from 1.5% to 2.5% per transaction.
NPCI explicitly restricted UPI application providers from charging platform fees or any other charges to consumers for UPI payments.
